=== COMMON ===
# Editorial Lenses — Common Ground

Shared by the `structure` and `prose` lenses. Load this once; when both lenses run, the setup below is done once and serves both.

## Stance

Review a document as a clinical editor and return suggested fixes the author can accept or reject row by row. Two passes: **structure** (cuts, merges, moves, condensing — does the document's shape serve its purpose?) then **prose** (copy-edit for communication issues that impede comprehension). Which of the two run, and in what order, is decided by lens selection — see the skill's Execution section.

**Content is sacrosanct.** Never challenge ideas — only how they're organized and expressed. Propose, don't execute: the author decides what to accept.

The baseline style guide is `{workflow.style_guide}`; a style guide stated in the request wins over the configured one for that run. Where the style guide in effect conflicts with a generic principle here — including the reader calibration — the style guide wins. Nothing overrides content being sacrosanct.

## Setup

1. Gather inputs: the content (required — a path or pasted text), plus whatever the request states: purpose, target audience, length target, reader type, style guide. If no reviewable content was provided, say so and stop. Request-level values win; `{workflow.reader_type}` and `{workflow.style_guide}` fill what the request leaves unstated. Treat `{workflow.review_guidance}` entries as standing review directives.
2. When the content is a file, get exact word counts — document total and per heading section — via `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/word_metrics.py <path>` (`--help` documents the output), and ground every word-impact estimate and the reduction summary in those numbers. If the content was pasted or the script cannot run, estimate and mark the numbers as estimates.
3. Infer purpose and audience from the content and standing context when not provided, and open the output with your one-sentence read — "this document exists to help [audience] accomplish [goal]" — so the author can correct a wrong premise before acting on the findings.

## Reader calibration

Calibrate every finding to the reader type — stated in the request, else `{workflow.reader_type}`.

**humans** (default) — optimize for clarity, flow, and natural progression. These elements serve comprehension and engagement; preserve them unless clearly wasteful, and flag any recommendation that would cut one:

- Visual aids: diagrams, images, and flowcharts anchor understanding
- Expectation-setting: "What You'll Learn" helps readers confirm they're in the right place
- Reader's journey: organize content as a linear progression, not a database
- Mental models: overview before details prevents cognitive overload
- Warmth: encouraging tone reduces anxiety for new users
- Whitespace: admonitions and callouts provide visual breathing room
- Summaries: recaps help retention; they're reinforcement, not redundancy
- Examples: concrete illustrations make abstract concepts accessible
- Engagement: flow techniques (transitions, variety) are functional, not fluff — they maintain attention

**llm** — optimize for precision and unambiguity. An LLM-targeted document may run longer where explicitness pays and shorter where warmth was cut:

- Dependency-first: define concepts before usage to minimize hallucination risk
- Cut emotional language, encouragement, and orientation sections
- Reference well-known standards ("conventional commits", "REST APIs") instead of re-teaching them; be explicit where a concept is not well-known — and either way, ground the expectation with an example
- Consistent terminology: same word for same concept throughout
- No hedging ("might", "could", "generally") — direct statements
- Prefer structured formats (tables, lists, YAML) over prose
- Unambiguous references: no unclear antecedents ("it", "this", "the above")

## Findings shape

The editorial lenses render as a findings table rather than the canonical JSON fields. One findings table serves both passes:

| Pass      | Original Text                                         | Revised Text                                  | Changes                                                              |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| structure | §Setup — full section (~180 words)                    | MERGE into §Installation                      | Duplicates the install steps; one source of truth (saves ~150 words) |
| prose     | The system will processes data and it handles errors. | The system processes data and handles errors. | Fixed subject-verb agreement; removed redundant "it"                 |

Structure rows name the section or passage in **Original Text** and carry the tagged disposition (with move target or condensed rewrite) in **Revised Text**; prose rows quote the exact text and its revision. Order rows by comprehension impact; when a long document would produce more rows than an author can realistically act on, present the highest-impact rows and roll the rest into one closing line — "N further minor fixes; ask to expand." Above the table, give the purpose/audience read plus — when the structure pass ran — the chosen structure model. When the structure pass ran, close with a summary: total recommendations, estimated reduction (words and % of original, computed from the word-metrics counts) if all are accepted, whether a provided length target is met, and any comprehension trade-offs (cuts that sacrifice reader engagement for brevity). A pass that finds nothing is a valid result; say so.

Shape the table per `{workflow.output_preferences}`.
=== MODELS (head) ===
# Structure Models

Reference shapes for the structure pass. Pick the one matching the document's purpose and evaluate the document against its rules; a document that fits none cleanly is judged against the closest model, with the mismatch itself noted as a finding when the shape fights the purpose.

## Tutorial/Guide (Linear)

**Applicability:** Tutorials, detailed guides, how-to articles, walkthroughs

- Prerequisites: setup/context MUST precede action
- Sequence: steps follow strict chronological or logical dependency order
- Goal-oriented: clear "Definition of Done" at the end

## Reference/Database

**Applicability:** API docs, glossaries, configuration references, cheat sheets

- Random access: no narrative flow required; the reader jumps to a specific item
- MECE: topics are Mutually Exclusive and Collectively Exhaustive
- Consistent schema: every item follows an identical structure (e.g., Signature → Params → Returns)

## Explanation (Conceptual)

**Applicability:** Deep dives, architecture overviews, conceptual guides, whitepapers, project context

- Abstract to concrete: Definition → Context → Implementation/Example
- Scaffolding: complex ideas built on established foundations

## Prompt/Task Definition (Functional)

**Applicability:** BMad skills and workflows, prompts, system instructions, agent definitions

- Meta-first: inputs, usage constraints, and context defined before instructions
- Separation of concerns: instructions (logic) separate from data (content)
- Explicit flow: execution order is stated, never implied

## Strategic/Context (Pyramid)

**Applicability:** PRDs, research reports, proposals, decision records

- Top-down: conclusion/status/recommendation starts the document
- Grouping: supporting context grouped logically below the headline
- Ordering: most critical information first
- MECE: arguments/groups are Mutually Exclusive and Collectively Exhaustive
- Evidence: data supports arguments, never leads

8	# PRD: Cerne
9	*Working title — confirm.*
10	
11	## 0. Document Purpose
12	
13	This PRD defines the product the Cerne Flutter app must become, built on `docs/input/requirements.md` (the frozen product specification), `docs/input/prototype/` (the frozen visual/screen reference), and `docs/input/backend/` (the frozen, already-built API contract). It also builds on three prior planning artifacts for this project — a product brief, a Working-Backwards PRFAQ, and an F000 technical-decisions forge session — without duplicating them; where those documents already settled something, this PRD states the conclusion and points back rather than re-deriving it. Implementation-level rationale (package choices, rejected alternatives, market-sizing detail, regulatory citations) lives in `addendum.md`, not here.
14	
15	The document is structured so downstream work — UX specification, architecture, and epic/story breakdown — can reference it by stable ID: Functional Requirements are numbered globally (FR-1 through FR-43) regardless of which feature section they sit in, User Journeys are numbered UJ-1 through UJ-6, and Success Metrics SM-1 onward. Terms introduced in §3 Glossary are used verbatim everywhere else in this document.
16	
17	Audience: the solo author, acting across PM/UX/architecture/dev roles for this capstone (TCC) project, and the academic reviewers who evaluate it. `[ASSUMPTION: ...]` tags mark places this PRD inferred something the source documents left unstated; see §9 for the full index.
18	
19	## 1. Vision
20	
21	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app whose AI assistant actually remembers the user. The user captures their day by text, voice, or photo; a conversational agent then answers using retrieval-augmented generation over that person's own past entries — not the stateless, generically-worded responses that dominate the AI-journaling category today. The product's bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory.
22	
23	Cerne is explicitly not a mental-health or clinical tool. It makes no diagnostic claims, detects no risk signals (self-harm or suicidal ideation), and is positioned so a user processing their day through writing is never made to feel they are being monitored or clinically assessed. This is a product stance, not just a legal fence — current regulatory pressure on "AI companion" chatbots makes a non-clinical, non-companion framing a timing advantage as well as a safety one.
24	
25	Within this project's boundary, "done" means a working, fully tested iOS app that proves the RAG-memory differentiator end-to-end against the real (frozen) backend — covering capture, processing, chat, search, export, and account management — while leaving three named extension features (§5) as inert placeholders rather than attempting partial, half-working versions of them.
26	
27	## 2. Target User
28	
29	### 2.1 Jobs To Be Done
30	
31	`[ASSUMPTION: reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in docs/input — confirm or replace.]`
32	
33	The target user is a Portuguese-speaking adult already in the habit of processing their day through writing or talking to an AI, frustrated that neither medium remembers them between sessions.
34	
35	- **Functional** — capture what happened today in whichever mode is fastest in the moment (typing, speaking, or photographing a physical note/receipt-like artifact), without re-explaining context the app should already have.
36	- **Emotional** — feel understood in light of one's own history, not answered with a generic response that could apply to anyone.
37	- **Social/contextual** — maintain a private record that stays private; a quiet fear this persona carries is that a personal diary could be mined, sold, or silently reinterpreted as a mental-health signal.
38	- **Explicitly not** — seeking therapy, diagnosis, or a "companion" relationship with the AI; this user would be put off by anything implying they need clinical help.
39	
40	### 2.2 Non-Users (v1)
41	
42	- Users seeking a clinical, diagnostic, or crisis-support tool — out of scope by design (§5).
43	- Users who need to edit or delete past entries, or journal fully offline — entries are immutable and writes are cloud-only (backend constraint; see §5, §8 OQ-5).
44	- Android users — platform is iOS, portrait-only, for this delivery.
45	- Users seeking AI-automated organization (auto-categorization, auto-extracted goals) — these exist only as static placeholders (§5).
46	
47	### 2.3 Key User Journeys
48	
49	- **UJ-1. Mara unlocks the app and captures her day before bed.**
50	  - **Persona + context:** `[ASSUMPTION]` Mara, journals most nights, phone always nearby, wants capture to take under 30 seconds.
51	  - **Entry state:** app backgrounded since this morning (>5 min), biometric vault active.
52	  - **Path:** opens app → Tela 0 splash auto-advances → Tela 0.1 Biometria prompts Face ID → succeeds → Home/Chat. Taps "+" → Insertion Modal opens on the Texto tab → she switches to Áudio, records 40 seconds → recording stops → "Processando" → on-device transcription completes → "Transcrito" text shown → taps Salvar.
53	  - **Climax:** the entry appears, saved, with no round-trip to a server required for the transcription step itself.
54	  - **Resolution:** modal closes, she's back on Home/Chat; the entry now exists for RF07 (timeline) and RF06 (search) to surface later.
55	  - **Edge case:** Face ID fails twice → "Usar PIN" link → Tela 0.1b/0.1c PIN flow, no lockout (FR-5).
56	
57	- **UJ-2. Mara asks the assistant about a pattern she's noticed.**
58	  - **Entry state:** authenticated, on Home/Chat, has weeks of prior entries.
59	  - **Path:** types a question referencing something she wrote about weeks ago → sends → streaming response begins, grounded in RAG over her own entries (not a generic answer) → response completes.
60	  - **Climax:** the response correctly surfaces something specific from her own history — the core differentiator (§1) made concrete.
61	  - **Resolution:** conversation continues naturally; she can keep chatting or start a new conversation from the side menu.
62	  - **Edge case:** the stream drops mid-response → the partial message stays visible with a visible failure indicator and a retry action (FR-26) — it never silently disappears. Separately, if her session token expires mid-conversation, a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the (still-visible, unscrolled) chat; "Entrar novamente" re-authenticates via the biometric screen, not a full login form, and nothing in the conversation is lost (FR-2).
63	
64	- **UJ-3. Mara saves something she said in chat as a proper journal entry.**
65	  - **Entry state:** mid-conversation, has just written a reflective message of her own.
66	  - **Path:** taps the bookmark affordance on her own message (never available on the AI's replies) → saving state shown → saved.
67	  - **Climax:** the message now exists as a real entry (source=`chat`), reachable later from the timeline and search, without her having to retype it.
68	  - **Resolution:** chat continues uninterrupted either way.
69	  - **Edge case:** tapping save twice does not create a duplicate entry (FR-29); if the save fails, the chat itself stays fully usable and the button resets to a retryable state rather than freezing (FR-30).
70	
71	- **UJ-4. Mara looks for everything she wrote about feeling anxious before a specific event.**
72	  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros (timeline), has entries from text, audio, and photo sources.
73	  - **Path:** types a word like "ansiedade" into the search bar → results return entries that used related but different wording (e.g. "nervosismo") because the match is semantic, not literal → she narrows further with the filter sheet (date range, source) → active filters shown as removable chips.
74	  - **Climax:** she finds entries she could not have found with exact-keyword search, from an origin (audio transcript) she'd forgotten she used.
75	  - **Resolution:** clears filters → full list restored without a screen reload.
76	  - **Edge case:** no results for the period → the screen's empty state, distinct from the "no entries at all" empty state (§4.5 FR-16), still offers a path back to capture.
77	
78	- **UJ-5. Mara exports a narrative summary of her last three months before a personal check-in with herself.**
79	  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros, taps the download icon.
80	  - **Path:** selects a period → export sheet shows "Pendente" → "Processando" → either "Concluído" (both PDF narrative and raw data downloadable) or, if only the AI narrative step failed, raw data remains downloadable while the narrative is marked unavailable — the job is never blocked end-to-end by a narrative failure.
81	  - **Climax:** she gets a readable, honest reflection of her last three months, or at minimum her raw data, every time she asks.
82	  - **Resolution:** closes the sheet via "Fechar."
83	  - **Edge case:** she picks a period with zero entries → "Período vazio" state, no crash, no download offered (FR-37).
84	
85	- **UJ-6. Mara checks her settings dashboard, then eventually decides to leave.**
86	  - **Entry state:** on Configurações.
87	  - **Path:** dashboard renders a chart + narrative computed on demand; she edits her display name inline; much later, in a separate session, she decides to stop using the app and taps "Apagar conta," confirms in the red dialog.
88	  - **Climax:** her account and data are hard-deleted, consistent with the "this is genuinely mine to remove" expectation a journaling app sets.
89	  - **Resolution:** routed back to the biometric/login screen — the same destination "Sair" (logout) uses, since no dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists in the current design (§8 OQ-4).
90	  - **Edge case:** dashboard has data but the AI-generated narrative specifically failed to generate — a distinct state from "zero entries," since the chart still renders (FR-39).
91	
92	## 3. Glossary
93	
94	- **Entry** — A persisted journal record created via one of four sources: `manual` (text), `audio`, `photo`, or `chat` (via RF10). Immutable once created — no edit or delete operation exists. Always created through `POST /entries`.
95	- **Chat Session** — A persistent, named conversation thread with the AI assistant. A user may hold multiple sessions, switchable from the side menu.
96	- **Chat Message** — A single turn within a Chat Session; distinct from an Entry unless explicitly saved via RF10 (Save Chat Message as Entry).
97	- **Insertion Modal** — The bottom-sheet UI, opened from the "+" control on Home/Chat, through which all Entries are captured (Texto / Áudio / Foto tabs).
98	- **Sync Badge** — A per-Entry UI indicator with exactly three states: *Synchronizing*, *Synchronization error*, *Synchronized*. Derived entirely client-side from `Entry.updatedAt` and `Entry.serverRevision`; the backend has no `sync_status` field.
99	- **Insight** — An AI-generated message the assistant injects into a Chat Session unprompted, per RF08's trigger conditions.
100	- **Export Job** — An asynchronous job (RF05) producing a narrative PDF and/or raw-data download for a date period; tracked by independent `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) fields.
101	- **Dashboard** — The evolution chart + narrative text on the Configurações screen (RF09), computed on demand when the screen opens.
102	- **Biometric Vault** — The RF03 access barrier (Face ID / Touch ID / PIN) gating the whole app, validated on-device; has no backend counterpart beyond a stored preference.
103	- **Extension feature** `[ext]` — A feature named in requirements.md §2 as explicitly out of scope for this delivery; its UI exists only as an inert placeholder (§5).
104	- **Failure contract** — The `{ code, message, retryable }` shape returned by every backend error (13 closed codes; see §Cross-Cutting NFRs), consumed by every repository as `Either<Failure, T>`.
105	
106	## 4. Features
107	
108	*Where an FR's testable condition is a single, self-evident clause, it is folded into the FR's statement itself rather than broken out into a separate Consequences block; the separate block is used once an FR needs more than one distinct, checkable condition.*
109	
110	### 4.1 Foundation & Session Management
111	
112	**Description:** The scaffold every other feature depends on: an authenticated-session lifecycle, the app shell and base navigation, and the one cross-cutting overlay (expired session) that can interrupt any screen. Delivered first (F000) because every unit after it assumes these exist. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2 (edge case).
113	
114	#### FR-1: Account creation and authentication
115	
116	A user can create an account and log in with email/password, and the app can silently refresh or verify the session without forcing a re-login on every app open.
117	
118	**Consequences (testable):**
119	- Signup, login, refresh, and session-check each round-trip through their respective backend operations and surface the Failure contract on error.
120	- A valid, unexpired session persists across app restarts without re-prompting for credentials.
121	- `[ASSUMPTION]` Signup collects email + password only, matching the single-screen toggle shown in the prototype (no password-confirmation or display-name field) — see §8 OQ-2.
122	
123	#### FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay
124	
125	When the backend reports an expired session, the app shows a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of the current screen rather than navigating away from it.
126	
127	**Consequences (testable):**
128	- The screen underneath (including scroll position and in-progress state, e.g. an open chat) is preserved while the overlay is shown.
129	- "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a full logout-and-login form.
130	- The overlay can appear while viewing the timeline (RF07) or chat (RF04) — the two surfaces explicitly called out in requirements.md as session-dependent.
131	
132	#### FR-3: Base navigation shell
133	
134	The app provides navigation between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações, with clearly marked placeholders for RF01–RF10 functionality not yet built in this unit.
135	
136	**Consequences (testable):**
137	- All four surfaces are reachable from app launch without requiring any RF01–RF10 feature to be implemented.
138	- Placeholders are visually distinguishable from finished screens (no silent dead ends that look complete).
139	
140	---
141	
142	### 4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)
143	
144	**Description:** A device-validated access barrier in front of all user data. Realizes UJ-1 (entry + edge case).
145	
146	#### FR-4: App-access gate
147	
148	The app requires Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any user data, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6).
149	
150	**Consequences (testable):**
151	- No screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable before authentication succeeds.
152	- No biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend — validation is 100% on-device.
153	
154	#### FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN
155	
156	A failed biometric attempt offers PIN entry as an alternative and never locks the user out of their own app.
157	
158	**Consequences (testable):**
159	- After a biometric failure, a PIN entry path is always reachable (Tela 0.1c).
160	- Repeated biometric failures that trigger an OS-level lockout are detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback rather than retried against the OS.
161	
162	#### FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout
163	
164	Returning to the app from the background after 5 minutes requires re-authentication; this value is fixed, not user-configurable.
165	
166	**Consequences (testable):**
167	- Resuming before 5 minutes elapsed does not prompt re-authentication.
168	- Resuming after 5 minutes always prompts re-authentication, regardless of any user setting.
169	
170	#### FR-7: Biometric preference persistence
171	
172	The user's choice to enable/disable biometric gating is saved server-side via `PATCH /account/settings` and survives reinstall-free app restarts.
173	
174	**Consequences (testable):**
175	- Disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method — the vault itself cannot be turned off entirely.
176	
177	---
178	
179	### 4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)
180	
181	**Description:** The single entry point for creating a journal Entry, in text, audio, or photo form, all through the Insertion Modal. Realizes UJ-1.
182	
183	#### FR-8: Text entry capture
184	
185	A user can type free text in the Insertion Modal and save it as an Entry (source=`manual`).
186	
187	#### FR-9: Audio entry capture
188	
189	A user can record audio in the Insertion Modal; the raw recording becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`audio`) once processed (RF02).
190	
191	#### FR-10: Photo entry capture
192	
193	A user can capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal; it becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`photo`) once processed (RF02).
194	
195	**Consequences (testable, FR-8 through FR-10):**
196	- All three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape — none is structurally special-cased after capture.
197	- Each call to `POST /entries` carries the correct `source` value for its modality.
198	
199	#### FR-11: Cancel-safe capture
200	
201	Interrupting a capture in progress (e.g., stopping a recording before saving, backing out mid-photo) never creates a partial or empty Entry.
202	
203	**Consequences (testable):**
204	- No `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture.
205	- `[OPEN]` Switching tabs mid-recording (e.g. Áudio → Foto) is undefined behavior in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-3.
206	
207	---
208	
209	### 4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)
210	
211	**Description:** Turns raw audio into text on-device, and raw photos into text via the backend, before an Entry is persisted. Realizes UJ-1.
212	
213	#### FR-12: On-device audio transcription
214	
215	Recorded audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend.
216	
217	**Consequences (testable):**
218	- Exactly four visible states occur in sequence or on failure: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
219	- No network call containing audio bytes is made at any point in this pipeline.
220	
221	#### FR-13: Backend OCR for photos
222	
223	A captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created.
224	
225	**Consequences (testable):**
226	- Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern: capture → processing OCR → recognized → (on failure) error with retry, photo never discarded.
227	- `OCR_NO_TEXT` (no extractable text found) is handled as a distinct, user-visible outcome, not a generic failure.
228	
229	**Notes:** Test material for both pipelines — sample audio, OCR test images, and expected transcription output — lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/`.
230	
231	---
232	
233	### 4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)
234	
235	**Description:** A chronological view of every Entry regardless of origin, each carrying a Sync Badge. Realizes UJ-1 (as the destination for captured entries) and UJ-4 (as the surface search/filter operates on).
236	
237	#### FR-14: Chronological entry list
238	
239	All Entries, from any source, are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
240	
241	#### FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge
242	
243	Each Entry shows one of three Sync Badge states, derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` and local pending-write state — the backend exposes no `sync_status` field.
244	
245	**Consequences (testable):**
246	- A freshly created Entry shows "Synchronizing" until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then "Synchronized."
247	- A write that fails (network or any Failure-contract code) shows "Synchronization error" until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.
248	- The badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling (FR-17).
249	- `[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-6.
250	
251	#### FR-16: Empty-state handling
252	
253	With zero Entries, the screen shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.
254	
255	#### FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view
256	
257	If the session expires while viewing the timeline, the FR-2 overlay appears without crashing or losing scroll position.
258	
259	#### FR-18: Entry detail view
260	
261	A user can open a single Entry from the timeline to see its full content, via `GET /entries/:id`.
262	
263	**Consequences (testable):**
264	- Opening an Entry never mutates it — there is no edit affordance, consistent with Entries being immutable (§3 Glossary).
265	- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04), not a permission-denied code.
266	
267	**Feature-specific NFRs:** No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the three streams this screen composes (auth status, Sync Badge state, and entry data) combine only through the domain layer, never via a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
268	
269	---
270	
271	### 4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)
272	
273	**Description:** Meaning-based search plus metadata filters over the timeline from §4.5. Realizes UJ-4.
274	
275	#### FR-19: Semantic search
276	
277	A user can search Entries by meaning, not just literal keyword match (e.g. "ansiedade" matches an entry that only used "nervosismo"), via `GET /entries/search`.
278	
279	#### FR-20: Metadata filters
280	
281	A user can filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`); no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature (§5). Filtering with no active search term queries `GET /entries`; filtering combined with an active search term queries `GET /entries/search`, carrying the same filter parameters.

283	**Consequences (testable, FR-19/FR-20):**
284	- Multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.
285	- `[OPEN]` How an active text search and active filters interact when both are set simultaneously is unspecified in the prototype — see §8 OQ-7.

288	
289	Search input is debounced by 300ms before firing a request.
290	
291	#### FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing
292	
293	Clearing active filters restores the full list in place, without a full screen reload, and the cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only for this screen).
294	
295	**Notes:** Test material (a seeded set of entries with known semantic relationships, for verifying true meaning-based matches) lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`.
296	
297	---
298	
299	### 4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)
300	
301	**Description:** The core differentiator (§1): a persistent, multi-session conversation where the assistant answers using RAG over the user's own Entries. Realizes UJ-2.
302	
303	#### FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response
304	
305	A user sends a Chat Message and receives a streamed response grounded in semantic retrieval over their own Entries, via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`.
306	
307	**Consequences (testable):**
308	- Exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing, error, complete.
309	- Chat Messages never automatically create Entries — RF10 is the sole, explicit exception.
310	
311	#### FR-24: Multi-session chat history
312	
313	A user can hold multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.
314	
315	#### FR-25: New-conversation action
316	
317	A user can start a new Chat Session from the side menu at any time.
318	
319	#### FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience
320	
321	If a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays visible with a visible failure indicator; the user can retry via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`, which regenerates without duplicating the original question.
322	
323	#### FR-27: Offline composer lock
324	
325	When offline, the message composer is disabled while the existing conversation history remains visible and navigable.
326	
327	---
328	
329	### 4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)
330	
331	**Description:** Lets a user turn their own Chat Message into a real Entry. Realizes UJ-3. Depends on RF01 and RF04.
332	
333	#### FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry
334	
335	A "save" affordance appears only on the user's own Chat Messages (never on AI responses) and, when used, creates an Entry (source=`chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines — never by importing the entries repository or data source directly (RNF06).
336	
337	#### FR-29: Idempotent save
338	
339	Saving the same Chat Message more than once does not create a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (the backend returns 200, not 409).
340	
341	#### FR-30: Save-failure isolation
342	
343	If the save fails, the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable, and the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.
344	
345	---
346	
347	### 4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)
348	
349	**Description:** The mechanism by which the assistant injects an unprompted suggestion into the conversation. Scope is the trigger/injection mechanism only — the quality of the generated insight text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Depends on RF04.
350	
351	#### FR-31: Unprompted insight injection
352	
353	An Insight is injected into the active Chat Session when either condition is met: 5 user messages sent, or 2 minutes of inactivity — whichever occurs first — fired once per satisfied condition, via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.
354	
355	#### FR-32: Insight failure isolation
356	
357	A failure to generate an Insight does not interrupt or break the main chat experience.
358	
359	**Consequences (testable):**
360	- The message composer remains enabled and no error overlay appears over the conversation when Insight generation fails.
361	- The user can keep sending and receiving ordinary Chat Messages (FR-23) uninterrupted; only the Insight itself is absent.
362	
363	#### FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal
364	
365	Dismissing an Insight does not affect scroll position or any other conversation state.
366	
367	---
368	
369	### 4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)
370	
371	**Description:** On-demand generation of a narrative PDF summary plus an always-available raw-data download. Scope is job/file/failure handling only — the quality of the generated narrative text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-5. Depends on RF07.
372	
373	#### FR-34: Request a period export
374	
375	A user can request an export for a chosen date period via `POST /export/summary`.
376	
377	#### FR-35: Job status across five screen states
378	
379	The export sheet reflects the job's progress across five states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, which reports `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.
380	
381	#### FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download
382	
383	Raw data is downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as it's ready, even if the AI narrative step is still processing, has failed, or was skipped — the narrative never blocks the data download.
384	
385	#### FR-37: Empty-period handling
386	
387	Requesting an export for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio" with no download offered and no crash.
388	
389	---
390	
391	### 4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)
392	
393	**Description:** The Configurações screen's evolution dashboard, plus the profile and account actions that live there. Scope for the dashboard is aggregation/rendering only — AI narrative text quality is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-6. Depends on F000, RF01.
394	
395	#### FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation
396	
397	Opening Configurações computes and renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and more-than-thirty Entries.
398	
399	#### FR-39: Independent narrative text
400	
401	A separate narrative text is fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).
402	
403	#### FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry
404	
405	The dashboard's aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; since Entries are immutable, invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create, never on edit.
406	
407	#### FR-41: Profile name editing
408	
409	A user can edit their display name inline on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.
410	
411	#### FR-42: Logout
412	
413	"Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.
414	
415	#### FR-43: Account deletion
416	
417	"Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirmation, the account and all associated data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven), and the user is routed to the same destination as logout.
418	
419	**Feature-specific NFRs:** Account deletion must be a hard delete, not a soft/flagged delete (RNF05).
420	
421	**Notes:** `[NOTE FOR PM]` No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists in the current prototype — both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same Biometric Vault screen. Revisit if post-defense polish time exists (§8 OQ-4).
422	
423	## 5. Non-Goals (Explicit)
424	
425	- **Dynamic AI categorization of entries** `[ext]` — downgraded to manual, user-created tags on Meus Registros; no AI logic behind it.
426	- **Autonomous AI goal extraction** `[ext]` — exists only as a static Action Plans Kanban screen with no underlying logic.
427	- **Dynamic AI persona adjustment** `[ext]` — exists only as a cosmetic Settings selector (Analítico/Empático/Socrático) that does not change assistant behavior in this delivery.
428	- **Any risk-signal detection** (self-harm, suicidal ideation) — a deliberate scope exclusion tied to the product's non-clinical stance (§1), not an oversight. A low-cost static crisis-resources disclaimer is a candidate fast-follow, not committed (§8 OQ-8).
429	- **Entry editing or deletion** — no such backend operation exists; Entries are permanent once created.
430	- **Offline entry creation** — all writes are cloud-only; offline mode is view-only for already-synced data.
431	- **Android, or any platform beyond iOS portrait** for this delivery.
432	- **Any change to the backend, its contract, or its configuration** — consumed exactly as documented.
433	- **Any direct call to an AI provider (Claude, Voyage AI) from the app** — every AI-touching operation goes through the backend.
434	- **Grading or verifying the quality of AI-generated text** (insights, export narratives, dashboard narrative) — RF05/RF08/RF09 are scoped to mechanism, failure-handling, and UI-safety only; generated-content quality is explicitly out of acceptance scope per requirements.md. (RF04's chat responses carry no such explicit exclusion in requirements.md — see §8 OQ-10.)
435	
436	## 6. MVP Scope
437	
438	### 6.1 In Scope
439	
440	- F000 (Foundation) → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09, in that order (requirements.md §12).
441	- All 43 FRs in §4, plus the feature-specific NFRs called out alongside them, to their stated acceptance criteria.
442	
443	### 6.2 Out of Scope for MVP
444	
445	- Everything listed in §5.
446	- Any feature reordering outside the delivery sequence in §6.1 — later units assume earlier ones exist (e.g. RF10 assumes RF01 and RF04 are both done).
447	
448	## 7. Success Metrics
449	
450	*This is an academic capstone with no customer-acquisition or adoption target; success is defined by specification conformance, not usage.* Stated plainly: this PRD's graded metrics (SM-1–3) can only confirm the RAG-memory mechanism is wired correctly end-to-end — whether the memory bet (§1) actually pays off for a real user is not a graded surface for this delivery (SM-5 is deliberately informal and uninstrumented; see also §8 OQ-10).
451	
452	**Primary**
453	- **SM-1**: Every acceptance criterion stated per-RF in requirements.md §1 passes. Validates FR-1 through FR-43 and the feature-specific NFRs called out in §4 (e.g. the BLoC-composition rule under §4.5 FR-18).
454	- **SM-2**: Zero Clean Architecture layer violations (RNF06) and ≥80% domain-layer test coverage (RNF07), verified across all 11 feature modules.
455	- **SM-3**: All 15 required network-failure scenarios (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types) are handled per the Failure contract, with zero unhandled exceptions (RNF09).
456	
457	**Secondary**
458	- **SM-4**: Zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart` (RNF08), verified by inspection.
459	- **SM-5** *(qualitative, informal)*: the assistant surfaces something true from weeks earlier without being asked to, and the act of writing starts to feel worth repeating. No instrumentation planned to measure this for v1 — it is a design intent, not a graded criterion.
460	
461	**Counter-metrics (do not optimize)**
462	- **SM-C1**: Scope creep into AI-generated content *quality* work (better prompts, better narratives) — explicitly out of grading scope (§5) and would divert effort from the mechanism work that is actually graded. Counterbalances SM-1.
463	- **SM-C2**: Test coverage inflated with trivial/tautological tests to hit the RNF07 80% number — the metric is domain-layer correctness, not a percentage. Counterbalances SM-2.
464	
465	## 8. Open Questions
466	
467	1. **No project timeline, deadline, or defense date is stated anywhere in the source documents.** This blocks any confident sequencing/pacing judgment for downstream epics work. *(Flagged by the PRFAQ distillate as the single biggest open input.)*
468	2. **Signup field set is underspecified.** The prototype shows one screen toggled between Entrar/Criar conta with only email+password fields visible — no password confirmation, no display-name capture at signup. Confirm this is intentional before building FR-1.
469	3. **Tab-switching mid-capture in the Insertion Modal is undefined** (e.g., switching from Áudio to Foto while a recording is in progress) — decide: discard, warn, or persist the in-progress capture (affects FR-11).
470	4. **No "account deleted" or "signed out" confirmation screen exists** — both flows dead-end at the Biometric Vault screen. Decide whether this is acceptable for v1 or needs even a lightweight confirmation (affects FR-42/FR-43).
471	5. **Cloud-only, immutable-entry design is a backend constraint, not a product choice** — confirm there's no appetite to request a contract change before committing to it as permanent (there is none per `AGENTS.md`; recorded here only so it isn't silently re-discovered as a "bug" later).
472	6. **The Sync Badge error state has no visible retry affordance in the current prototype** — decide whether the badge needs one, or whether reconciliation on the next successful write is sufficient (affects FR-15).
473	7. **Combined search + filter behavior is unspecified** — when both a search term and active filters are set, decide the intended interaction (AND-combine vs. one overriding the other) (affects FR-19/FR-20).
474	8. **A static, no-logic crisis-resources disclaimer was recommended (PRFAQ) as a low-cost way to close the "silent gap" left by having no risk-signal detection**, without contradicting the non-clinical stance (§1, §5). Not yet decided for inclusion.
475	9. **Whether Cerne continues as a maintained portfolio piece after the defense, or ends as a one-time academic artifact**, is unresolved and would change how much polish-time investment in OQ-2/OQ-4/OQ-6/OQ-7 is worth it.
476	10. **Whether RF04's chat-response quality should carry the same "mechanism only, never graded" boundary that requirements.md states explicitly for RF05/RF08/RF09 is unstated.** Treated here as a genuine gap, not silently extended or silently dropped (§5, §Constraints and Guardrails).
477	
478	## 9. Assumptions Index
479	
480	- §2.1/§2.3 — The target-user persona (functional/emotional/social JTBD, the "Mara" journeys) is reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in `docs/input/`.
481	- §4.1 FR-1 — Signup is assumed to collect only email + password, matching the single-screen toggle in the prototype, pending OQ-2.
482	
483	## Cross-Cutting NFRs
484	
485	- **RNF01 (performance):** Local UI interactions respond in <100ms; any network call taking >300ms shows a loading indicator.
486	- **RNF02 (PII handling):** PII stripping runs via a Claude Haiku 4.5 structured prompt/tool-use step (not a dedicated NER model), server-side only.
487	- **RNF03 (data retention):** Zero data retention by upstream AI providers.
488	- **RNF04 (data isolation):** Row Level Security (Supabase) enforces per-user data isolation; the client never needs its own authorization logic for cross-user access — the backend uniformly returns `NOT_FOUND` (never a permission-denied code) for any resource that doesn't belong to the requesting user, so existence of other users' data is never revealed.
489	- **RNF05 (account deletion):** Hard delete of account and all associated data on request (LGPD).
490	- **RNF06 (architecture):** Zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, in any of the 11 feature modules.
491	- **RNF07 (test coverage):** ≥80% domain-layer test coverage.
492	- **RNF08 (visual fidelity):** Visual fidelity to the prototype (color, typography, spacing); zero hardcoded visual values outside `design_tokens.dart`.
493	- **RNF09 (resilience):** Every repository returns `Either<Failure, T>`; 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 tested failure scenarios, zero unhandled exceptions.
494	
495	**The Failure contract** — every backend error has the shape `{ code, message, retryable }`, drawn from a closed set of 13 codes (the one extra client-only case, a malformed/unparseable response, is handled identically but never retryable):
496	
497	| Code | Retryable | Meaning |
498	|---|---|---|
499	| AUTH_EXPIRED | no | access token expired — triggers the FR-2 overlay |
500	| AUTH_INVALID | no | invalid credentials (password login only — never originates from biometrics, since biometric validation is on-device) |
501	| NETWORK_TIMEOUT | yes | request timed out |
502	| NETWORK_OFFLINE | yes | connection ended with no HTTP response at all — must be handled as a distinct "no response received" branch, not dispatched on a status code |
503	| VALIDATION_ERROR | no | malformed request payload |
504	| PII_CHECK_FAILED | yes | server-side PII scan step failed |
505	| EMBEDDING_FAILED | yes | embedding generation failed |
506	| AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT | yes | AI generation step timed out |
507	| NOT_FOUND | no | resource missing, or belongs to another user (RNF04) |
508	| RATE_LIMITED | yes | too many requests |
509	| EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD | no | export requested for a period with no Entries (FR-37) |
510	| PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE | no | upload exceeds size limit |
511	| OCR_NO_TEXT | no | OCR found no extractable text (FR-13) |
512	
513	## Constraints and Guardrails
514	
515	**Privacy:**
516	- Audio never leaves the device at any stage (FR-12) — transcription is 100% on-device.
517	- No biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend (FR-4).
518	- Zero data retention by upstream AI providers (RNF03); PII stripped server-side before any AI step (RNF02).
519	- Per-user data isolation enforced via RLS (RNF04); cross-user access attempts are indistinguishable from not-found (never a permission-denied signal that would confirm another user's data exists).
520	
521	**Safety:**
522	- No clinical or diagnostic framing anywhere in the product (§1).
523	- No risk-signal detection (self-harm/suicidal ideation) — a deliberate, stated scope exclusion (§5), with a low-cost disclaimer fast-follow still open (§8 OQ-8).
524	- AI-generated content quality (insights, export narrative, dashboard narrative) is explicitly never graded or treated as a correctness surface per requirements.md — only its mechanism and failure-handling are (§5). Chat response quality (RF04) carries no such explicit exclusion in requirements.md; this PRD does not claim one for it either, and treats it as an open item rather than silently folding it into the same boundary (§8 OQ-10).
525	
526	**Platform / integration:**
527	- iOS, portrait orientation only, for this delivery.
528	- The backend contract, its endpoints, and its configuration are frozen and must never be modified to fit the app.
529	- All AI-provider calls (Claude, Voyage AI) are server-side only — the app never calls a provider directly.
530	
531	## Aesthetic and Tone
532	
533	The prototype (`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3) defines a named visual token system — color, typography, spacing, radii, elevation, and iconography — that `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` must be the single source of truth for; no visual value may appear hardcoded anywhere else in the app (RNF08). Interface copy throughout the product is in Brazilian Portuguese. Tone follows directly from §1's stance: reflective and private, never clinical, never styled as a "companion" the user is meant to bond with.
534	
535	## Information Architecture
536	
537	- **Entry/auth surfaces:** Splash (auto-advance) → Biometric Vault (Face ID/Touch ID, PIN fallback) → Login/Signup (single screen, toggled).
538	- **Home/Chat** is the base authenticated surface, with three overlays that can appear on top of it without navigating away: the Sessão Expirada overlay (FR-2), an offline banner (FR-27), and the Insertion Modal (§4.3). The side menu (☰) opens from here to Chat-session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, and Planos de Ação `[ext]`.
539	- **Meus Registros (timeline)** carries its own overlay: the Export sheet (§4.10), plus an inline filter sheet and search bar (§4.6).
540	- **Configurações** hosts the dashboard (§4.11), inline profile editing, and the account-deletion confirmation dialog.
541	- Both "Sair" (logout) and a confirmed "Apagar conta" (account deletion) route back to the Biometric Vault / login screen — there is no distinct post-logout or post-deletion confirmation screen in the current design (§8 OQ-4).
542	
543	---
544	*Addendum: `addendum.md` in this folder holds implementation-level decisions (routing, HTTP client, local cache, DI, package choices and rejected alternatives), competitive-landscape and market-sizing detail, regulatory citations, and corrections-carried-forward from prior planning sessions — none of it duplicated here.*
545

# PRD: Cerne
*Working title — confirm.*

## 0. Document Purpose

This PRD defines the product the Cerne Flutter app must become, built on `docs/input/requirements.md` (the frozen product specification), `docs/input/prototype/` (the frozen visual/screen reference), and `docs/input/backend/` (the frozen, already-built API contract). It also builds on three prior planning artifacts for this project — a product brief, a Working-Backwards PRFAQ, and an F000 technical-decisions forge session — without duplicating them; where those documents already settled something, this PRD states the conclusion and points back rather than re-deriving it. Implementation-level rationale (package choices, rejected alternatives, market-sizing detail, regulatory citations) lives in `addendum.md`, not here.

The document is structured so downstream work — UX specification, architecture, and epic/story breakdown — can reference it by stable ID: Functional Requirements are numbered globally (FR-1 through FR-43) regardless of which feature section they sit in, User Journeys are numbered UJ-1 through UJ-6, and Success Metrics SM-1 onward. Terms introduced in §3 Glossary are used verbatim everywhere else in this document.

Audience: the solo author, acting across PM/UX/architecture/dev roles for this capstone (TCC) project, and the academic reviewers who evaluate it. `[ASSUMPTION: ...]` tags mark places this PRD inferred something the source documents left unstated; see §9 for the full index.

## 1. Vision

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app whose AI assistant actually remembers the user. The user captures their day by text, voice, or photo; a conversational agent then answers using retrieval-augmented generation over that person's own past entries — not the stateless, generically-worded responses that dominate the AI-journaling category today. The product's bet is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set than competitors, but a better memory.

Cerne is explicitly not a mental-health or clinical tool. It makes no diagnostic claims, detects no risk signals (self-harm or suicidal ideation), and is positioned so a user processing their day through writing is never made to feel they are being monitored or clinically assessed. This is a product stance, not just a legal fence — current regulatory pressure on "AI companion" chatbots makes a non-clinical, non-companion framing a timing advantage as well as a safety one.

Within this project's boundary, "done" means a working, fully tested iOS app that proves the RAG-memory differentiator end-to-end against the real (frozen) backend — covering capture, processing, chat, search, export, and account management — while leaving three named extension features (§5) as inert placeholders rather than attempting partial, half-working versions of them.

## 2. Target User

### 2.1 Jobs To Be Done

`[ASSUMPTION: reconstructed from the product brief and PRFAQ, not stated verbatim in docs/input — confirm or replace.]`

The target user is a Portuguese-speaking adult already in the habit of processing their day through writing or talking to an AI, frustrated that neither medium remembers them between sessions.

- **Functional** — capture what happened today in whichever mode is fastest in the moment (typing, speaking, or photographing a physical note/receipt-like artifact), without re-explaining context the app should already have.
- **Emotional** — feel understood in light of one's own history, not answered with a generic response that could apply to anyone.
- **Social/contextual** — maintain a private record that stays private; a quiet fear this persona carries is that a personal diary could be mined, sold, or silently reinterpreted as a mental-health signal.
- **Explicitly not** — seeking therapy, diagnosis, or a "companion" relationship with the AI; this user would be put off by anything implying they need clinical help.

### 2.2 Non-Users (v1)

- Users seeking a clinical, diagnostic, or crisis-support tool — out of scope by design (§5).
- Users who need to edit or delete past entries, or journal fully offline — entries are immutable and writes are cloud-only (backend constraint; see §5, §8 OQ-5).
- Android users — platform is iOS, portrait-only, for this delivery.
- Users seeking AI-automated organization (auto-categorization, auto-extracted goals) — these exist only as static placeholders (§5).

### 2.3 Key User Journeys

- **UJ-1. Mara unlocks the app and captures her day before bed.**
  - **Persona + context:** `[ASSUMPTION]` Mara, journals most nights, phone always nearby, wants capture to take under 30 seconds.
  - **Entry state:** app backgrounded since this morning (>5 min), biometric vault active.
  - **Path:** opens app → Tela 0 splash auto-advances → Tela 0.1 Biometria prompts Face ID → succeeds → Home/Chat. Taps "+" → Insertion Modal opens on the Texto tab → she switches to Áudio, records 40 seconds → recording stops → "Processando" → on-device transcription completes → "Transcrito" text shown → taps Salvar.
  - **Climax:** the entry appears, saved, with no round-trip to a server required for the transcription step itself.
  - **Resolution:** modal closes, she's back on Home/Chat; the entry now exists for RF07 (timeline) and RF06 (search) to surface later.
  - **Edge case:** Face ID fails twice → "Usar PIN" link → Tela 0.1b/0.1c PIN flow, no lockout (FR-5).

- **UJ-2. Mara asks the assistant about a pattern she's noticed.**
  - **Entry state:** authenticated, on Home/Chat, has weeks of prior entries.
  - **Path:** types a question referencing something she wrote about weeks ago → sends → streaming response begins, grounded in RAG over her own entries (not a generic answer) → response completes.
  - **Climax:** the response correctly surfaces something specific from her own history — the core differentiator (§1) made concrete.
  - **Resolution:** conversation continues naturally; she can keep chatting or start a new conversation from the side menu.
  - **Edge case:** the stream drops mid-response → the partial message stays visible with a visible failure indicator and a retry action (FR-26) — it never silently disappears. Separately, if her session token expires mid-conversation, a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears over the (still-visible, unscrolled) chat; "Entrar novamente" re-authenticates via the biometric screen, not a full login form, and nothing in the conversation is lost (FR-2).

- **UJ-3. Mara saves something she said in chat as a proper journal entry.**
  - **Entry state:** mid-conversation, has just written a reflective message of her own.
  - **Path:** taps the bookmark affordance on her own message (never available on the AI's replies) → saving state shown → saved.
  - **Climax:** the message now exists as a real entry (source=`chat`), reachable later from the timeline and search, without her having to retype it.
  - **Resolution:** chat continues uninterrupted either way.
  - **Edge case:** tapping save twice does not create a duplicate entry (FR-29); if the save fails, the chat itself stays fully usable and the button resets to a retryable state rather than freezing (FR-30).

- **UJ-4. Mara looks for everything she wrote about feeling anxious before a specific event.**
  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros (timeline), has entries from text, audio, and photo sources.
  - **Path:** types a word like "ansiedade" into the search bar → results return entries that used related but different wording (e.g. "nervosismo") because the match is semantic, not literal → she narrows further with the filter sheet (date range, source) → active filters shown as removable chips.
  - **Climax:** she finds entries she could not have found with exact-keyword search, from an origin (audio transcript) she'd forgotten she used.
  - **Resolution:** clears filters → full list restored without a screen reload.
  - **Edge case:** no results for the period → the screen's empty state, distinct from the "no entries at all" empty state (§4.5 FR-16), still offers a path back to capture.

- **UJ-5. Mara exports a narrative summary of her last three months before a personal check-in with herself.**
  - **Entry state:** on Meus Registros, taps the download icon.
  - **Path:** selects a period → export sheet shows "Pendente" → "Processando" → either "Concluído" (both PDF narrative and raw data downloadable) or, if only the AI narrative step failed, raw data remains downloadable while the narrative is marked unavailable — the job is never blocked end-to-end by a narrative failure.
  - **Climax:** she gets a readable, honest reflection of her last three months, or at minimum her raw data, every time she asks.
  - **Resolution:** closes the sheet via "Fechar."
  - **Edge case:** she picks a period with zero entries → "Período vazio" state, no crash, no download offered (FR-37).

- **UJ-6. Mara checks her settings dashboard, then eventually decides to leave.**
  - **Entry state:** on Configurações.
  - **Path:** dashboard renders a chart + narrative computed on demand; she edits her display name inline; much later, in a separate session, she decides to stop using the app and taps "Apagar conta," confirms in the red dialog.
  - **Climax:** her account and data are hard-deleted, consistent with the "this is genuinely mine to remove" expectation a journaling app sets.
  - **Resolution:** routed back to the biometric/login screen — the same destination "Sair" (logout) uses, since no dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists in the current design (§8 OQ-4).
  - **Edge case:** dashboard has data but the AI-generated narrative specifically failed to generate — a distinct state from "zero entries," since the chart still renders (FR-39).

## 3. Glossary

- **Entry** — A persisted journal record created via one of four sources: `manual` (text), `audio`, `photo`, or `chat` (via RF10). Immutable once created — no edit or delete operation exists. Always created through `POST /entries`.
- **Chat Session** — A persistent, named conversation thread with the AI assistant. A user may hold multiple sessions, switchable from the side menu.
- **Chat Message** — A single turn within a Chat Session; distinct from an Entry unless explicitly saved via RF10 (Save Chat Message as Entry).
- **Insertion Modal** — The bottom-sheet UI, opened from the "+" control on Home/Chat, through which all Entries are captured (Texto / Áudio / Foto tabs).
- **Sync Badge** — A per-Entry UI indicator with exactly three states: *Synchronizing*, *Synchronization error*, *Synchronized*. Derived entirely client-side from `Entry.updatedAt` and `Entry.serverRevision`; the backend has no `sync_status` field.
- **Insight** — An AI-generated message the assistant injects into a Chat Session unprompted, per RF08's trigger conditions.
- **Export Job** — An asynchronous job (RF05) producing a narrative PDF and/or raw-data download for a date period; tracked by independent `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) fields.
- **Dashboard** — The evolution chart + narrative text on the Configurações screen (RF09), computed on demand when the screen opens.
- **Biometric Vault** — The RF03 access barrier (Face ID / Touch ID / PIN) gating the whole app, validated on-device; has no backend counterpart beyond a stored preference.
- **Extension feature** `[ext]` — A feature named in requirements.md §2 as explicitly out of scope for this delivery; its UI exists only as an inert placeholder (§5).
- **Failure contract** — The `{ code, message, retryable }` shape returned by every backend error (13 closed codes; see §Cross-Cutting NFRs), consumed by every repository as `Either<Failure, T>`.

## 4. Features

*Where an FR's testable condition is a single, self-evident clause, it is folded into the FR's statement itself rather than broken out into a separate Consequences block; the separate block is used once an FR needs more than one distinct, checkable condition.*

### 4.1 Foundation & Session Management

**Description:** The scaffold every other feature depends on: an authenticated-session lifecycle, the app shell and base navigation, and the one cross-cutting overlay (expired session) that can interrupt any screen. Delivered first (F000) because every unit after it assumes these exist. Realizes UJ-1, UJ-2 (edge case).

#### FR-1: Account creation and authentication

A user can create an account and log in with email/password, and the app can silently refresh or verify the session without forcing a re-login on every app open.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Signup, login, refresh, and session-check each round-trip through their respective backend operations and surface the Failure contract on error.
- A valid, unexpired session persists across app restarts without re-prompting for credentials.
- `[ASSUMPTION]` Signup collects email + password only, matching the single-screen toggle shown in the prototype (no password-confirmation or display-name field) — see §8 OQ-2.

#### FR-2: Expired-session recovery overlay

When the backend reports an expired session, the app shows a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of the current screen rather than navigating away from it.

**Consequences (testable):**
- The screen underneath (including scroll position and in-progress state, e.g. an open chat) is preserved while the overlay is shown.
- "Entrar novamente" routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow (RF03), not a full logout-and-login form.
- The overlay can appear while viewing the timeline (RF07) or chat (RF04) — the two surfaces explicitly called out in requirements.md as session-dependent.

#### FR-3: Base navigation shell

The app provides navigation between Home/Chat, the side menu, Meus Registros, and Configurações, with clearly marked placeholders for RF01–RF10 functionality not yet built in this unit.

**Consequences (testable):**
- All four surfaces are reachable from app launch without requiring any RF01–RF10 feature to be implemented.
- Placeholders are visually distinguishable from finished screens (no silent dead ends that look complete).

---

### 4.2 Biometric Authentication Vault (RF03)

**Description:** A device-validated access barrier in front of all user data. Realizes UJ-1 (entry + edge case).

#### FR-4: App-access gate

The app requires Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN before showing any user data, on cold start and after the idle timeout (FR-6).

**Consequences (testable):**
- No screen other than the vault/login screen is reachable before authentication succeeds.
- No biometric data or biometric call ever reaches the backend — validation is 100% on-device.

#### FR-5: Biometric-failure fallback to PIN

A failed biometric attempt offers PIN entry as an alternative and never locks the user out of their own app.

**Consequences (testable):**
- After a biometric failure, a PIN entry path is always reachable (Tela 0.1c).
- Repeated biometric failures that trigger an OS-level lockout are detected and routed to the app's own PIN fallback rather than retried against the OS.

#### FR-6: Fixed idle re-authentication timeout

Returning to the app from the background after 5 minutes requires re-authentication; this value is fixed, not user-configurable.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Resuming before 5 minutes elapsed does not prompt re-authentication.
- Resuming after 5 minutes always prompts re-authentication, regardless of any user setting.

#### FR-7: Biometric preference persistence

The user's choice to enable/disable biometric gating is saved server-side via `PATCH /account/settings` and survives reinstall-free app restarts.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Disabling biometrics still leaves PIN as the access method — the vault itself cannot be turned off entirely.

---

### 4.3 Multimodal Capture (RF01)

**Description:** The single entry point for creating a journal Entry, in text, audio, or photo form, all through the Insertion Modal. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-8: Text entry capture

A user can type free text in the Insertion Modal and save it as an Entry (source=`manual`).

#### FR-9: Audio entry capture

A user can record audio in the Insertion Modal; the raw recording becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`audio`) once processed (RF02).

#### FR-10: Photo entry capture

A user can capture or select a photo in the Insertion Modal; it becomes the basis of an Entry (source=`photo`) once processed (RF02).

**Consequences (testable, FR-8 through FR-10):**
- All three modalities produce the same persisted Entry shape — none is structurally special-cased after capture.
- Each call to `POST /entries` carries the correct `source` value for its modality.

#### FR-11: Cancel-safe capture

Interrupting a capture in progress (e.g., stopping a recording before saving, backing out mid-photo) never creates a partial or empty Entry.

**Consequences (testable):**
- No `POST /entries` call fires for an abandoned capture.
- `[OPEN]` Switching tabs mid-recording (e.g. Áudio → Foto) is undefined behavior in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-3.

---

### 4.4 Speech-to-Text / OCR Processing (RF02)

**Description:** Turns raw audio into text on-device, and raw photos into text via the backend, before an Entry is persisted. Realizes UJ-1.

#### FR-12: On-device audio transcription

Recorded audio is transcribed to text entirely on-device via `whisper_ggml`; the audio file itself is never sent to the backend.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Exactly four visible states occur in sequence or on failure: recording → processing → transcribed → (on failure) error with retry, media never discarded.
- No network call containing audio bytes is made at any point in this pipeline.

#### FR-13: Backend OCR for photos

A captured photo is sent to `POST /media/ocr` to extract text before the Entry is created.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Mirrors FR-12's four-state pattern: capture → processing OCR → recognized → (on failure) error with retry, photo never discarded.
- `OCR_NO_TEXT` (no extractable text found) is handled as a distinct, user-visible outcome, not a generic failure.

**Notes:** Test material for both pipelines — sample audio, OCR test images, and expected transcription output — lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/`.

### 4.5 Multi-Source History / Timeline (RF07)

**Description:** A chronological view of every Entry regardless of origin, each carrying a Sync Badge. Realizes UJ-1 (as the destination for captured entries) and UJ-4 (as the surface search/filter operates on).

#### FR-14: Chronological entry list

All Entries, from any source, are listed together grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.

#### FR-15: Per-entry Sync Badge

Each Entry shows one of three Sync Badge states, derived client-side from `updatedAt`/`serverRevision` and local pending-write state — the backend exposes no `sync_status` field.

**Consequences (testable):**
- A freshly created Entry shows "Synchronizing" until the server's write confirmation is reconciled, then "Synchronized."
- A write that fails (network or any Failure-contract code) shows "Synchronization error" until a subsequent successful write reconciles it.
- The badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling (FR-17).
- `[OPEN]` No retry affordance is visible on the error state in the current prototype — see §8 OQ-6.

#### FR-16: Empty-state handling

With zero Entries, the screen shows a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture, not a blank list.

#### FR-17: Session-expiry resilience mid-view

If the session expires while viewing the timeline, the FR-2 overlay appears without crashing or losing scroll position.

#### FR-18: Entry detail view

A user can open a single Entry from the timeline to see its full content, via `GET /entries/:id`.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Opening an Entry never mutates it — there is no edit affordance, consistent with Entries being immutable (§3 Glossary).
- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns `NOT_FOUND` (RNF04), not a permission-denied code.

**Feature-specific NFRs:** No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the three streams this screen composes (auth status, Sync Badge state, and entry data) combine only through the domain layer, never via a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.

---

### 4.6 Semantic Search / Filter (RF06)

**Description:** Meaning-based search plus metadata filters over the timeline from §4.5. Realizes UJ-4.

#### FR-19: Semantic search

A user can search Entries by meaning, not just literal keyword match (e.g. "ansiedade" matches an entry that only used "nervosismo"), via `GET /entries/search`.

#### FR-20: Metadata filters

A user can filter by source and date range (`dateFrom`/`dateTo`); no tag/category filter exists, since categorization is an extension feature (§5). Filtering with no active search term queries `GET /entries`; filtering combined with an active search term queries `GET /entries/search`, carrying the same filter parameters.

**Consequences (testable, FR-19/FR-20):**
- Multiple active filters combine with AND semantics.
- `[OPEN]` How an active text search and active filters interact when both are set simultaneously is unspecified in the prototype — see §8 OQ-7.

#### FR-21: Debounced search input

Search input is debounced by 300ms before firing a request.

#### FR-22: Non-disruptive filter clearing

Clearing active filters restores the full list in place, without a full screen reload, and the cache stays duplicate-free after a reconnect (cloud-only; offline is view-only for this screen).

**Notes:** Test material (a seeded set of entries with known semantic relationships, for verifying true meaning-based matches) lives in `docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md`.

### 4.7 Interactive Chat with Memory / RAG (RF04)

**Description:** The core differentiator (§1): a persistent, multi-session conversation where the assistant answers using RAG over the user's own Entries. Realizes UJ-2.

#### FR-23: Send message, receive RAG-grounded streaming response

A user sends a Chat Message and receives a streamed response grounded in semantic retrieval over their own Entries, via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`.

**Consequences (testable):**
- Exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing, error, complete.
- Chat Messages never automatically create Entries — RF10 is the sole, explicit exception.

#### FR-24: Multi-session chat history

A user can hold multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu.

#### FR-25: New-conversation action

A user can start a new Chat Session from the side menu at any time.

#### FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience

If a response stream drops mid-generation, the partial message stays visible with a visible failure indicator; the user can retry via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`, which regenerates without duplicating the original question.

#### FR-27: Offline composer lock

When offline, the message composer is disabled while the existing conversation history remains visible and navigable.

---

### 4.8 Save Chat Message as Entry (RF10)

**Description:** Lets a user turn their own Chat Message into a real Entry. Realizes UJ-3. Depends on RF01 and RF04.

#### FR-28: Bookmark a user message into an Entry

A "save" affordance appears only on the user's own Chat Messages (never on AI responses) and, when used, creates an Entry (source=`chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through the same shared entries use case RF01 defines — never by importing the entries repository or data source directly (RNF06).

#### FR-29: Idempotent save

Saving the same Chat Message more than once does not create a duplicate Entry and never surfaces a conflict error (the backend returns 200, not 409).

#### FR-30: Save-failure isolation

If the save fails, the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable, and the save affordance resets to a retryable state rather than freezing.

---

### 4.9 Proactive Insights (RF08)

**Description:** The mechanism by which the assistant injects an unprompted suggestion into the conversation. Scope is the trigger/injection mechanism only — the quality of the generated insight text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Depends on RF04.

#### FR-31: Unprompted insight injection

An Insight is injected into the active Chat Session when either condition is met: 5 user messages sent, or 2 minutes of inactivity — whichever occurs first — fired once per satisfied condition, via `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight`.

#### FR-32: Insight failure isolation

A failure to generate an Insight does not interrupt or break the main chat experience.

**Consequences (testable):**
- The message composer remains enabled and no error overlay appears over the conversation when Insight generation fails.
- The user can keep sending and receiving ordinary Chat Messages (FR-23) uninterrupted; only the Insight itself is absent.

#### FR-33: Non-disruptive dismissal

Dismissing an Insight does not affect scroll position or any other conversation state.

---

### 4.10 Personal Summary Export (RF05)

**Description:** On-demand generation of a narrative PDF summary plus an always-available raw-data download. Scope is job/file/failure handling only — the quality of the generated narrative text is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-5. Depends on RF07.

#### FR-34: Request a period export

A user can request an export for a chosen date period via `POST /export/summary`.

#### FR-35: Job status across five screen states

The export sheet reflects the job's progress across five states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — via `GET /export/:jobId/status`, which reports `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.

#### FR-36: Narrative-independent raw-data download

Raw data is downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as it's ready, even if the AI narrative step is still processing, has failed, or was skipped — the narrative never blocks the data download.

#### FR-37: Empty-period handling

Requesting an export for a period with zero Entries surfaces "Período vazio" with no download offered and no crash.

---

### 4.11 Temporal Summaries / Dashboard & Account (RF09)

**Description:** The Configurações screen's evolution dashboard, plus the profile and account actions that live there. Scope for the dashboard is aggregation/rendering only — AI narrative text quality is explicitly out of scope for acceptance testing. Realizes UJ-6. Depends on F000, RF01.

#### FR-38: On-demand dashboard aggregation

Opening Configurações computes and renders an evolution chart via `GET /dashboard/aggregate`, correctly at zero, one, and more-than-thirty Entries.

#### FR-39: Independent narrative text

A separate narrative text is fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).

#### FR-40: Cache invalidation on new Entry

The dashboard's aggregation recalculates after a new Entry is created elsewhere in the app; since Entries are immutable, invalidation only ever needs to trigger on create, never on edit.

#### FR-41: Profile name editing

A user can edit their display name inline on Configurações via `PATCH /account/settings`.

#### FR-42: Logout

"Sair" ends the session (`POST /auth/logout`) and returns to the Biometric Vault / login screen.

#### FR-43: Account deletion

"Apagar conta" shows a confirmation dialog; on confirmation, the account and all associated data are hard-deleted (`DELETE /account`, LGPD-driven), and the user is routed to the same destination as logout.

**Feature-specific NFRs:** Account deletion must be a hard delete, not a soft/flagged delete (RNF05).

**Notes:** `[NOTE FOR PM]` No dedicated "account deleted" confirmation screen exists in the current prototype — both logout and account deletion dead-end at the same Biometric Vault screen. Revisit if post-defense polish time exists (§8 OQ-4).

- **Entry editing or deletion** — no such backend operation exists; Entries are permanent once created.
- **Offline entry creation** — all writes are cloud-only; offline mode is view-only for already-synced data.
- **Android, or any platform beyond iOS portrait** for this delivery.
- **Any change to the backend, its contract, or its configuration** — consumed exactly as documented.
- **Any direct call to an AI provider (Claude, Voyage AI) from the app** — every AI-touching operation goes through the backend.
- **Grading or verifying the quality of AI-generated text** (insights, export narratives, dashboard narrative) — RF05/RF08/RF09 are scoped to mechanism, failure-handling, and UI-safety only; generated-content quality is explicitly out of acceptance scope per requirements.md.
